reason: Runnable (gp/python, enumeration of ~p points of F_V, p<=2^16 n=2 and p<=2^11 n=3, well under 20 CPU-min) and metrics are structural counts, not wall time. But as written it does not discriminate. (1) Ratio |Tr(F_V)|/r with |F_V|~p and |E(F_p)|~p is the image of a ~p-set under a homomorphism into a ~p-group; any random-function model gives ~1-1/e=0.63, inside the prediction [0.5,1], so prediction_if_true is near-vacuous; the null 'random subset of equal size' is ambiguous (random subset of E(F_p) gives ratio 1 trivially, random subset of E(F_{p^n}) pushed through Tr is the meaningful control). (2) Relation counts at m=2: R in E(F_p), F_V in E(F_{p^n}); expected decompositions ~|F_V|^2/p^n = p^(2-n): ~1 per target at n=2, ~1/p at n=3, so '5% of random' is unmeasurable at n=3 and needs hundreds of targets at n=2; the stated m=2 cell cannot test n=3. (3) V=cF_p with c in F_p is degenerate (points lie in E(F_p) or its twist, trace is nP or 0, i.e. the twist closure); must require c not in F_p and report the c in F_p case as a separate control. (4) Prediction_if_false ('trace collapses') has no mechanism for generic c (Frob moves x to c^p t, c^(p^2) t, so Tr sums points on different lines); outcome is essentially predetermined by counting, so the experiment confirms accounting rather than testing a hypothesis. Tr is a homomorphism, so Transport-conservation (|kappa|^(m-1)) already predicts every count; the toy can only confirm bookkeeping. Scaling: the claim B>=p is the coverage threshold |F_V|^m >= p^n at m=n, an exact counting statement that is p-independent in form, so toy results do scale as accounting; they say nothing about solving cost/degree at n=131 or ECCp-131 (n=1, where there is no extension to embed into). Expected class 'accounting' is correct and the experiment should be treated as a sanity check, not evidence for or against a new route.
fix: Redesign as a coverage-threshold test with a Poisson null. Setup (gp, PARI ffgen/ellinit; or python3+cypari2): E over F_p, n in {2,3}, F_{p^n}; V = F_p-span of k generic elements (k=1,2), none in F_p for k=1; F_V = {P in E(F_{p^n}) affine : x(P) in V}. Targets: >=2000 random R in E(F_p). Counts: ordered m-decompositions R=P_1+..+P_m with P_i in F_V, using hash of pair sums (n=2,m=2: p up to 2^16; n=3,m=3: p<=2^11 via hash of pair sums |F_V|^2~4e6 for k=1; k=2,n=3,m=2: p<=2^9). Metrics (all counted, no time): (a) B=|F_V|; (b) mean decompositions per R vs prediction B^m/(m!?)/p^n (use ordered count B^m/|E(F_{p^n})|*|E(F_p)|-corrected: expected = B^m/|E(F_{p^n})| * [E(F_p)-density factor] i.e. fit constant); (c) coverage fraction Pr[R has >=1 decomposition] and its sigmoid in log(B^m/p^n); (d) |Tr(F_V)|/|E(F_p)| and the multiplicity histogram of Tr. Null arms: N1 = random subset of E(F_{p^n}) of size B pushed through Tr and the same decomposition count; N2 = same V' with other generic c (V-independence); N3 = degenerate c in F_p (expect collapse: image in E(F_p) with trace nP or 0, counts differ), as positive control that the harness can detect collapse. Pass for 'true': counts and coverage within 3 sigma (Poisson) of N1 across >=6 values of p and the coverage threshold at B^m/p^n ~ O(1), i.e. B ~ p^(n/m) -> B>=p at m=n; image fraction within 3 sigma of 1-exp(-B/|E(F_p)|). Pass for 'false': any statistically significant deviation from N1 for generic c (>3 sigma, reproducible across p), or coverage at B^m/p^n << 1. Drop the 'within [0.5,1]' and '5% of random' criteria; drop m=2 at n=3. State beforehand that a 'true' outcome is accounting-only and implies no route.
collisions: Transport conservation (Tr is a homomorphism, kernel size p^(n-1)-ish, |kappa|^(m-1))
Twist closure (c in F_p degenerate case)
